name: Kane Rava Fry
subtitle: ladyfish rubbed in red chilli paste and shallow fried in a sandy semolina crust

ingredients.qty: 8 whole ladyfish, cleaned and slit down both sides
ingredients.note: kane is the local name; small pomfret or mackerel fillets fry the same way

ingredients.qty: 8 dried, soaked 20 minutes in warm water

ingredients.note: this is wheat semolina, so the dish is not gluten-free
mixed into the rava, it keeps the crust crisp as the fish cools
fried in the last of the oil and scattered over

prepNotes: Rinse the fish, pat it thoroughly dry inside and out, and score the thicker fish twice on each side.
Grind the masala first, then marinate the fish for 30 minutes in the fridge. Much longer and the lemon starts cooking the flesh.
Spread the rava on a wide plate so you can press the fish into it in one motion.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, turmeric and pepper with 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a thick paste.
Mix in the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt, then rub the paste into the fish, working it into the slits.
Marinate 30 minutes in the fridge while you get the pan and the rava plate ready.
Stir the rice flour into the rava on a wide plate.
Heat 3 tbsp coconut oil in a flat tawa until a pinch of rava dropped in sizzles immediately.
steps.tip: If the oil is not hot enough the crust drinks it and goes soggy instead of crisping.

steps.text: Press each fish into the rava on both sides, shake off the loose grains and lay it straight into the pan.
steps.tip: Coat one fish at a time. Rava left sitting on a wet marinade turns to paste.

steps.text: Fry 4 minutes on the first side without touching it, until the crust is set and deep red-gold at the edges.
steps.tip: Moving it early is what tears the crust off. Wait until it releases from the pan on its own.

steps.text: Flip once and fry 3 minutes on the second side, adding the remaining oil around the edge of the pan as needed.
Fry the curry leaves in the last of the hot oil for 15 seconds and scatter them over the fish.
Drain on a rack, not on paper, and serve hot with raw onion and lemon.
steps.tip: A rack keeps the underside crisp; paper traps steam and softens it.

storage: Eat within the hour. This is a dish that does not keep. Leftovers will sit 1 day refrigerated and are best crisped up in a dry pan, never in a microwave.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
